docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation site. This site contains:

  • Usage instructions to get started
  • Realistic examples for common tasks
  • A comprehensive, auto-generated API reference

If you add Python packages/modules under src/ or the repository root, the API page will populate automatically via mkdocstrings after running the generation script.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Ensure Python 3.8+ is installed
  2. Install docs tooling: pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material mkdocstrings[python]
  3. Generate API page: python scripts/discover_python_modules.py
  4. Serve docs locally: mkdocs serve
  5. Build static site: mkdocs build

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This page is generated from source code via mkdocstrings.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thank you for helping improve this project. This guide explains how to work with the docs and APIs.

docs.title: Docs workflow
docs.text:
1. Install tooling:
  2. python3 -m pip install --user mkdocs mkdocs-material mkdocstrings[python]
  3. Generate API page:
  4. python3 scripts/discover_python_modules.py
  5. Preview locally:
  6. python3 -m mkdocs serve
  7. Build static site:
  8. python3 -m mkdocs build

docs.title: Adding/Updating APIs
docs.text:
• Place Python modules under src/ (recommended) or the repository root.
  • Public members (not starting with _) are documented automatically by mkdocstrings.
  • Re-run scripts/discover_python_modules.py after adding new modules.

docs.title: Writing examples
docs.text: • Add end-to-end examples to docs/examples.md or create new pages under docs/ and link them from mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• Use Google-style docstrings for functions, classes, and methods.
  • Prefer descriptive names and clear parameter/return descriptions.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Below are end-to-end examples demonstrating common scenarios. Replace placeholder names with your actual package and modules once available.

docs.title: Example: Initialize and run a job
docs.text:
from myapp import Client

client = Client(api_key="test_key")
result = client.run_job(params={"size": 10})
print(result)

docs.title: Example: Handling errors
docs.text:
from myapp import Client, MyAppError

client = Client(api_key="test_key")
try:
    client.run_job(params={"size": -1})
except MyAppError as exc:
    print(f"Failed to run job: {exc}")

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: This section describes how to install, configure, and use the project.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Use your preferred package manager. For Python projects:

pip install -e .

If your project is not yet packaged, use it directly from source and ensure dependencies are installed.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Document environment variables and configuration files here. Example:

  • MYAPP_ENV: Environment name (e.g., dev, prod)
  • MYAPP_LOG_LEVEL: Logging level (e.g., INFO, DEBUG)

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
If you expose a CLI, provide examples:

myapp run --config config.yaml

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
If the project is used as a library, provide import and minimal usage examples:

from myapp import Client

client = Client(api_key="...")
client.do_work()
